nodes.recap: chapter header + bridge from c20's monolith down to camp at its base, then the night valley from the platform: hundreds of fires, drums, singing, the Jeorghe memory, and the small hidden campfire
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 21          |
-------------------------------


$CThe light goes gray around the platform as you start back down from
the outcrop, and whatever daylight the crossing cost you, the climb
down finishes spending.##

Nobody argues about where to make camp.# The base of the same rock,
out of sight of the valley below, will do.##

Later, with the dark properly down, you go up the rock one last
time and stand on the platform on your own, looking out.# The
valley has become a scatter of fires, hundreds of them, spread from
one side of it to the other, and around each of them men are eating
and drinking, and if you hold still and listen long enough you can
catch a drum, and voices singing.##

You have seen this before.# You saw it your first night on this
planet, when a horde welcomed you in its own particular way, and
you find you are thinking about Jeorghe's face, and deciding that
nothing in this world or the other one could ever make you want to
see it again.##

You go back down to the others.##

The fire they have built is small, and it sits in the middle of
foliage thick enough that no part of it can be seen from the valley
below.# They caught something before sundown, animals not unlike
cats, and you all eat them in silence and without much appetite.

nodes.recap: the plan for entering the city [DECISION x2: how Kriss deflects Corolla, and how he answers Efeliah] - then the dissociation, 'then it's decided', and dreamless sleep

dialogues.precomment:
A few minutes after the last of it is gone, Ef is the one who
speaks first.
dialogues.line: We have to work out a plan for getting into the city.

We move under the dark.# A little before the sun comes up.# That
is the smallest risk.

dialogues.precomment: Corolla lets that sit for about a second and a half.
dialogues.line:
And then there is the other problem.# Once we are standing at the
gates, how do we get them opened?# Do you want to go and knock and
say: friends?

replies.line: Put it off. You'll think about it when you're there.
Tell her the gates will not be what stops you.
Say nothing, and keep looking into the dark.

dialogues.precomment: Corolla sighs, and turns back to the fire.
dialogues.line:
And crossing the camp?# How do we do that without being seen or
heard?# It is not a courtyard.# Once we are out of the forest it is
a couple of kilometres in the open...

I can feel the difference between a waking mind and a sleeping
one.

replies.line: Then that settles it: she guides.
Say nothing, and let it stand.

dialogues.line: Two kilometres.# Not one stone to hide behind.

Exactly.# Not so much as a hole to crawl into.# And if we snap one
twig they will be on us in their hundreds inside of seconds.
dialogues.comment:
The silence comes down over all of you.# You sit and watch the
fire, the only source of light and of sound in the world just now,
with its low, steady crackling.##

You could not describe your own state of mind if somebody asked you
to.# You cannot get your attention to hold on to anything real, you
feel dissociated from it, set very slightly to one side of it, and
the only thing anywhere in your head is the city.

dialogues.precomment:
After a while you stand up and start toward the tent.# Before you
disappear into it, you say:
dialogues.comment:
You say it in the same absent tone you have used all evening.##

You lie down on your pallet, and every thought leaves your head at
once, and a deep sleep takes you.# A sleep without dreams.

dialogues.line: We'll think about that when we're there...
The gates will not be what stops us.

dialogues.precomment:
You do not answer her.# You keep your eyes on the dark past the
fire, where the trees begin.
You nod, once, and leave it there.

nodes.recap: dream-flight hub 1: the forest. Spokes 50 (nothing stirs) and 51 (the call). Advance gated on having heard the call
nodes.text:
$CIt is still dark.# The dark will hold a while longer yet.##

You are moving, silent, invisible, through vegetation thicker than
any you have ever seen, and it does not touch you, and you do not
touch it.

choices.desc: Look at what is moving in the forest around you.
Look out toward the city, far off in the dark.

nodes.recap: spoke: nothing stirs, not even the night animals notice him
nodes.text:
$CNothing is moving.##

Nothing at all, anywhere around you.# Not a branch, not a leaf, and
not one of the night animals that ought to be awake at this hour
and ought, at the very least, to startle.##

They do not startle.# Not one of them is able to tell that anything
has gone past.

nodes.recap: spoke: the slow aching sound from the palace, the single lit window - a song, a lament, a call
nodes.text:
$CYou look out past the trees, down the length of the valley.##

The city is a pale shape in the dark, and in the palace at the
heart of it a single high window is still lit, and out of that
window comes a sound.##

It is slow, and it aches, and it crosses two kilometres of sleeping
army to reach you as clearly as if it were being made an arm's
length from your ear.##

It could be a song.# It could be a lament.# It could be a call.

nodes.recap: dream-flight hub 2: over the sleeping army. Spokes 52 (the stripped ground) and 53 (first light behind him)
nodes.text:
$CYou come out of the trees, over open ground, and beneath you the
camp begins.##

You feel them before you see them: thousands of men asleep under
you, and among them the smaller, harder points of the ones who are
awake and standing guard.# Not one of them can see you.# Not one of
them can hear you.# You slip into the shadows and through their
breathing, and the only trace of yourself you leave anywhere is in
the oblivion of the sleepers.

choices.desc: Look at what the army has done to the ground.

nodes.recap: spoke: sailing like a ghost ship over ground stripped bare by the army
nodes.text:
$CYou sail over it like some spectral ship: ground stripped down to
nothing by an army of brutes whose heads, so far as you can feel
them from up here, hold nothing at all but death, and violence, and
rot.##

What was forest yesterday is bare earth tonight, all the way to the
walls.

nodes.recap: spoke: looking back without turning, the first light, moving faster
nodes.text:
$CWithout turning, you look behind you.##

There is a faint glow along the edge of the world back there, the
kind that runs ahead of the day-star, and it is not faint enough.##

You move faster.

nodes.recap: dream-flight hub 3: beneath the walls, no gates. Spoke 54 (moonstone walls)
nodes.text:
$CYou are beneath the walls.##

There is no time to find the gates.##

$c<<And what would they be for?>>$C##

$CThe voice is stronger here.

nodes.recap: spoke: the walls shining like moonstones, evanescent and ethereal
nodes.text:
$CIn the pale, indistinct glow that goes before the day they shine
like moonstones, evanescent, ethereal.##

And at the same time they are exactly what they have always been:
mighty bulwarks, immense and old, rising sheer out of the floor of
the valley.

nodes.recap: dream-flight hub 4: dancing up the wall and over the roofs. Spoke 55 (the trembling window)
nodes.text:
$CYou go up the face of the wall as though you were dancing, prisoner
of nothing in this world but that song, and you crest it, and the
sleeping city opens underneath you.##

You pass over it like a cloud, over lovely roofs that are still
holding a little of yesterday's warmth, leaving the army and its
threat behind you.##

The first rays of the sun are arriving now, refracted, washing the
whole landscape in a light that belongs to dreams.

choices.desc: Look at the lit window in the palace.

nodes.recap: spoke: the light in the high window trembling as if it senses him
nodes.text:
$CThe high window is close now, and closer every moment, and the
light inside it is trembling.##

It trembles the way a candle does when a door opens somewhere else
in the house.# It trembles as though it can feel you coming.

nodes.recap: dream-flight hub 5: the palace gardens and the white stair. Spoke 56 (sleeping trees, murmuring fountains)
nodes.text:
$CYou come down into the gardens of the palace.##

Ahead of you a great white staircase rises, its marble gone soft,
almost liquid, in that milky light.

choices.desc: Stay a moment among the trees and the fountains.

nodes.recap: spoke: the enchanting sleeping trees and the mysterious murmur of the fountains
nodes.text:
$CThe trees here are enchanting and still fast asleep, and between
them the fountains go on with their mysterious murmuring in the
dark, to nobody at all.

nodes.recap: the figure at the top of the stair whispering his name, then the first ray of sun and the light taking everything
nodes.text:
$CHalfway up, you see it.##

Or you believe you see it: a figure at the top of the staircase,
arms held open, whispering, and what it is whispering is your
name.##

In that same instant the first ray of the sun goes through the sky
like a burning dart and breaks across those steps, and the steps
catch it and run like molten lava, and the light grows, and grows,
until it is blinding, until it is irresistible, until everything
has been swallowed by it and there is nothing left around you at
all but heat, and light.

nodes.recap: waking physically in the palace gardens, the friends waking around him, and the stair from the dream in front of him
nodes.text:
$CYou open your eyes slowly.# The daylight blinds you.##

You look around, and it takes you no time at all to work out that
you are not in your tent.##

A wonderful garden lies in front of you, full of fountains and
flowers and trees swaying gently under a light breeze, and on the
ground around you your friends are still lying where they went to
sleep, and they are waking now, one by one.##

You turn, and you are dumbstruck.##

The staircase you saw last night is standing right in front of
you.##

$c<<It cannot have been only a dream.##

Or am I still dreaming?>>$C

nodes.recap: the companions wake in the gardens with no idea how [DECISION: how Kriss answers, or fails to] - then the climb begins

dialogues.precomment:
Corolla is on her feet before any of the rest of you, knife in
hand, reading walls that are not the walls she went to sleep
inside.

Smiurl has both hands over his face and is going through four
colours without settling on any of them.
dialogues.line: The walls...# the army...# how are we inside?

replies.line: Say you are not sure you are awake.

dialogues.precomment:
Efeliah has not said anything.# She is standing very still with her
eyes on the top of the staircase.##

In that half-conscious state of doubt you start up the steps, and
you feel your own unease and your own excitement climbing with you,
one step at a time.##

You do not even notice that the others have begun to follow.

dialogues.line: I saw that staircase last night.# I was standing right here.
I am not sure I am awake yet.

dialogues.precomment: You do not answer him.# You are not certain you could.

nodes.recap: the top of the stair: the veiled atrium - end of chapter, c22 opens inside the hall
nodes.text:
$CFrom partway up you can already make out a vast atrium at the head
of the stair, cut off from the outside by veils that fall from a
very high ceiling and dance in the breath of air that moves over
this land like something alive.##

You come to the end of the staircase.##
